names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 decembrie, «Sfântul Mucenic Bonifatie».

Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιοι Βονιφάτιος και Αγλαΐα η Ρωμαία», with the rank word left off. The page glosses the name itself, «(από το λατινικό bonus + fatus) = ο ευλογημένος».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s first heading for 19. децембар ст. ст., „Свети мученик Бонифатије.“ — «Свети» is “saint” and not a rank and «мученик» is the rank `martyr` the folder already carries, so BRIEF-SERBIAN §6 strips both and the bare forename is the whole of what the heading gives him. Measured before it was written: ten characters, above the width the gate indexes, and no other folder holds this string — the other Bonifaces the corpus keeps carry no Serbian form at all.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding menologion day (28 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 decembrie — «Sfântul Mucenic Bonifatie»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Βονιφάτιος και Αγλαΐα η Ρωμαία»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day both folders already keep, and the entry is the same pair: the rich Roman woman and the steward of her property, who sinned together, repented, and parted — he to martyrdom at Tarsus of Cilicia, she to the relief of the poor. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. **The two sources differ in what they make of the household and the page states its own century.** doxologia makes Boniface the household servant of Aglaia, daughter of a proconsul named Acacius; saint.gr makes him «γραμματέας της περιουσίας της Αγλαΐας και επόπτης των κτημάτων της», secretary of her property and overseer of her estates, says nothing of her father, and says of her only that she belonged to the class of the noble and rich Roman women; and it opens «Οι Άγιοι Βονιφάτιος και Αγλαΐα έζησαν τον 3ο μ.Χ. αιώνα», which is recorded in `dates` for folders that held none. Boniface's page head adds «(; - 290)». saint.gr is as plain about the sin as doxologia and gives it a reason, quoting Luke 15:10 on the joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, and it has them confess the moral fall to a spiritual priest. It names Rome and Tarsus of Cilicia; no coordinate is proposed. It lists portions of Boniface's relic at the monasteries of Panteleimon on the Holy Mountain, Giromeri of Filiates, Phaneromeni of Salamis, Saint Nicholas of Andros and Saint Cyprian of Fyli in Attica, which is not drafted. It prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both naming Boniface — the apolytikion names Aglaia too, as the one to whom he gave his body — and an oikos and a kathisma, which are kinds the schema does not hold.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.01.2026 (19. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Бонифатије.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, and the longest of the four. Identified on the whole dossier and not on the name: the slave of the rich and dissolute Аглаида at Rome, sent to Asia to buy martyrs’ relics for her house, who said at parting that she might one day receive his own body instead, who came to Тарс, saw the Christians under torture, repented, cried „И ја сам хришћанин!“, was scourged, had molten lead poured into his mouth without harm and was beheaded — and whose body his slaves carried back to Rome, where an angel told Аглаида to receive him. «Пострада свети Бонифатије 290. године» AGREES EXACTLY with the 290 this folder already holds, and the third-century floruit beside it, so `dates` is untouched. Аглаида’s own repentance, her almsgiving and her fifteen years of bitter penitence are in this entry too, BUT SHE TAKES NO SERBIAN ROW: the heading names only him, and a name inside a body is not a heading. The `related` row the two already carry in both directions stands. The Serbian form is the heading’s bare forename, «Свети» being “saint” and «мученик» the rank; measured first, no other folder in the corpus holds that string. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026).

floruit.note: saint.gr's opening sentence for the pair: «Οι Άγιοι Βονιφάτιος και Αγλαΐα έζησαν τον 3ο μ.Χ. αιώνα.» The folder held no dates before this reading.

death.note: saint.gr's page head for him, «Αγιος Βονιφατιος (; - 290)». Its narrative gives no year at all, saying only that he died a martyr's death for the faith at Tarsus of Cilicia; the century in the floruit is the page's own opening sentence for him and Aglaia together.

hymns.text: Μαρτύρων τὴν εὔκλειαν ἰχνηλατήσας θερμῶς, Χριστὸν ὡμολόγησας ἐπὶ ἀπίστων στερρῶς, σοφὲ Βονιφάτιε· ὅθεν καθάπερ πλοῦτον ἀδαπάνητον, μάρτυς, δέδωκάς σου τὸ σῶμα τῇ σεμνῇ Ἀγλαΐᾳ· ἐξ οὗ τῷ κόσμῳ πηγάζει ῥώσις καὶ ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε. It names Boniface, and names Aglaia as the one to whom his body was given, so it is taken into both folders, on the page of «Άγιοι Βονιφάτιος και Αγλαΐα η Ρωμαία».

english.text: Warmly tracking out the good fame of the martyrs, you confessed Christ steadfastly before unbelievers, O wise Boniface; wherefore, O martyr, you gave your body to the modest Aglaia as a wealth that is never spent, and from it strength and mercy well up for the world.

hymns.text: Ἱερεῖον ἄμωμον, ἐθελουσίως, σεαυτὸν προσήγαγες, τῷ ἐκ Παρθένου διὰ σέ, τεχθῆναι μέλλοντι Ἅγιε, στεφανηφόρε σοφὲ Βονιφάτιε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον. It names Boniface alone, so it is taken into his folder only, on the page of «Άγιοι Βονιφάτιος και Αγλαΐα η Ρωμαία».

english.text: A spotless victim, you offered yourself willingly to him who for your sake was about to be born of the Virgin, O holy one, O crown-bearing and wise Boniface.
